The event brings together the 32nd annual Association of American Railroads Research Review and the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers Vehicular Technology Society (IEEE VTS) INNOVARail program under the theme of “200 Years of Railway Innovation.” The Research Review will include presentations, technical discussions, and panels showcasing results from the AAR’s Strategic Research Initiatives Program. The event will also include a walk of the Facility for Accelerated Service Testing (FAST) Track and an MxV Rail experience. A special focus in 2027 will be on crosstie challenges and innovations. INNOVARail includes a multidisciplinary focus on railroad research, technology, and development, including academic research, industry innovation, and workforce development. candidates.title: More than half of Senate now sponsoring short line tax credit bill
candidates.excerpt: WASHINGTON — More than half the members of the U.S. Senate have now signed on as co-sponsors of a key bill for short line railroads, the American Short Line and Regional Railroad Association has announced. The Railroad Track Maintenance Credit Modernization bill, S. 1532, would update what is commonly known as the 45G tax credit, which dates to 2005 and provides an incentive for railroads to invest their funds in track and bridge improvements. The credit is currently limited to a 40-cent credit for each dollar of track improvement, up to a limit of $3,500 per mile. The bill seeks to increase the credit to $6,100 per mile and index it to the rate of inflation going forward. ASLRRA President Chuck Baker called the credit “a critical tool for short line railroads” in a press release. “But the credit has not kept pace with inflation, diminishing its impact over time, and it excludes short lines established since 2015.” The bill was introduced last year by Sen. candidates.excerpt: A good friend dared Matt Hewitt to give model railroading a try. candidates.title: How reliable in predicting spot prices is box ship utilisation?
candidates.excerpt: Blanked sailings on the rise, with container spot rates on a gentle decline Container spot freight rates on the transpacific and Asia-Europe trades saw another week of gentle ... The relationship between vessel utilisation and container spot freight rates is markedly different on the transpacific and Asia-Europe trades. New analysis from Sea-Intelligence raises questions over how reliably capacity utilisation can predict pricing. The analyst found a strong correlation between utilisation and spot rates on the transpacific, where freight rates rise sharply once vessel utilisation exceeds 90%. However, the relationship is considerably weaker on Asia-Europe, where transhipment activity and geopolitical disruptions complicate the traditional supply-demand equation. Sea-Intelligence compared Drewry’s World Container Index (WCI) spot rates with demand data from Container Trade Statistics (CTS) and capacity figures from its own Trade Capacity Outlook database. Atlantic & Great Lakes will be based in Rochester, N.Y., and led by Chief Executive Bill Keough, who has been with G&W for eight years and most recently served as regional senior vice president. Canyon & Cascade Transportation Inc., which will be comprised of G&W operations in Washington, Oregon, California, Arizona, and New Mexico. candidates.title: AAR Reports Weekly Rail Traffic for the Week Ending November 7, 2026
candidates.excerpt: The Association of American Railroads (AAR) reported U.S. rail traffic for the week ending November 7, 2026. For this week, total U.S. weekly rail traffic was 526,283 carloads and intermodal units, up 6.6 percent compared with the same week last year. Total carloads for the week ending November 7 were 227,914 carloads, up 1.3 percent compared with the same week in 2025, while U.S. weekly intermodal volume was 298,369 containers and trailers, up 11.0 percent compared to 2025. Seven of the 10 carload commodity groups posted an increase compared with the same week in 2025. They included motor vehicles and parts, up 1,443 carloads, to 15,283; metallic ores and metals, up 1,215 carloads, to 20,274; and forest products, up 774 carloads, to 8,401. Commodity groups that posted decreases compared with the same week in 2025 were coal, down 698 carloads, to 56,997; grain, down 589 carloads, to 23,708; and nonmetallic minerals, down 561 carloads, to 32,376.
